outcome: A permanent that loses banding also loses all bands-with-other abilities.
An attacking band is legal only if it holds at least one creature with banding and at most one without it, or, for bands-with-other, only creatures of the named quality.
note: Declaring a band is a choice; the composition limits are the engine's verdict on that declaration.

outcome: All creatures in an attacking band must attack the same player, planeswalker or battle.
An announced attacking band persists for the rest of combat even if banding is later removed from its members.
An attacking creature removed from combat also leaves its band, so it no longer shares blocked status.
Creatures in a band keep their own abilities and remain separate permanents; banding shares and removes no abilities.
When one attacking creature in a band becomes blocked, every other creature in the band becomes blocked by that same blocker, regardless of evasion.
When an effect would make one member of a band blocked, the entire band becomes blocked.
When an attacker is blocked by a banding creature, the defending player rather than the attacking player divides its combat damage among its blockers.
note: Names the assignment choice together with its observable consequence.

outcome: When a blocker blocks a banding creature, the active player rather than the defending player divides the blocker's combat damage among the creatures it blocks.
